question: Why can momentum improve gradient descent, especially in ravines or noisy settings?
direct_answer: It smooths updates by accumulating past gradients, helping speed up consistent directions and damp oscillations.
expanded_answer: Momentum adds a velocity-like state that keeps part of the previous update, so the optimizer does not react only to the current gradient. In directions where gradients keep pointing similarly, momentum builds speed and can move faster through shallow valleys. In directions with alternating signs, it averages out noise and reduces zig-zagging, which makes optimization more stable.
key_points: Uses past gradients to build velocity
Damps oscillations in noisy or narrow valleys
Acts as a smoother than plain GD
common_wrong_ideas: Momentum is just a bigger learning rate
Momentum always guarantees better final accuracy
